Sean — good call flagging. Quick guidance and a recommended concession plan below. I ran a quick unit-econ calc (see attached model):

Proposed commercial approach (recommended):
- Offer A (pilot-first): 30% off list for months 1–3, then 15% off list months 4–6 if they sign a 6-month pilot commitment. This is framed as a time-limited pilot discount to protect long-term price integrity.
- Offer B (credits): $10k platform credit + 20% off API token list for first 3 months if they prefer credits for bookkeeping.
- Add-on: 100k free embedding units for first month and 90 days of retained logs for debugging (we default to no-retention for customer data, but will enable read-only debug logs with PII redaction on request).

Unit economics notes:
- Our incremental cost after batching/kv-cache is ~ $0.011–$0.014 per 1k generated tokens at 2–6M monthly volume (varies by model context length and request distribution).
- With the 30% pilot discount, our effective price to the customer would be roughly in the $0.02–$0.035 per 1k bucket — competitive with public effective rates after OpenAI credits are accounted for.
- If procurement pushes for parity with an advertised OpenAI effective rate, propose a rebate structure tied to sustained 6-month volume rather than a straight list cut — this preserves short-term margins and gives us a path to recover if usage drops.

Proc/Legal: Priyom, if you can confirm we can provide a signed attestation for no-retention for the pilot and the guardrails needed, we'll include that as a contract appendix. Aditya — flag if the credit + discount combo goes below our approved floor.

I attached a quick competitor model (competitor_pricing_model.xlsx) with scenario runs. We should be able to land this without a deep discount if we bundle embedding credits and operational support.
